evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 字形; 形義通解; 《說文》; cited older uses
evidence.text: The entry displays one small-seal form, one bronze example, four manuscript examples, and one other form; it displays no oracle-bone example. Its account analyzes the bronze form as 水 plus sound element 曷 and reports it used for 竭, “water dried up/exhausted,” in the Zhongshan King Fanghu inscription and a Mawangdui Laozi manuscript. It quotes the Shuowen gloss 盡也 and 从水、曷聲. Separately, it cites the Shijing line 苟無飢渴 for thirst, a Tang Bai Juyi use for dryness, and a Gongyang zhuan use glossed 急 (urgent). These source assertions do not establish all semantic bridges or earliest surviving physical witnesses.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫: 渴

evidence.source: 教育部《異體字字典》 (Taiwan Ministry of Education)
evidence.field: 說文釋形; pronunciations and definitions; form table
evidence.text: The entry quotes the Shuowen analysis 盡也。从水，曷聲 and records the readings jié, kě, and hé with separate glosses: dried up/exhausted, thirsty/urgent, and a Chu-Yue regional word for reverse-flowing water. Its form table labels a Shuowen Da-Xu small-seal item and notes that bronze-script compilations are not publicly available on this entry. This is lexicographic evidence and does not independently verify a bronze graph.
evidence.title: [A02267] 渴 - 教育部《異體字字典》

evidence.field: kMandarin for U+6E34, U+66F7, and U+6C35
evidence.text: Attempted the exact official character lookup pages for 渴 (U+6E34), 曷 (U+66F7), and 氵 (U+6C35), including the useutf8 parameter; all were inaccessible through the web tool. The invocation supplied local Unihan rows: 渴 kě, 曷 hé, and 氵 shui. Those exact local rows are harness-provided evidence, not a verified character-specific upstream page. The supplied local Baxter–Sagart rows give 渴 *Nə-[k]ʰˤat (MC khat) and 曷 *[g]ˤat (MC hat); the initials differ in this system, while the coda material overlaps. These readings qualify the sound comparison but do not alone prove a phonetic role.

gaps: No direct image is selected. The exact Commons description page, official imageinfo API response, and direct SVG all failed to open; the candidate's pixels, attribution chain, and license metadata cannot be verified. The supplied local glyph file and manifest are leads only.
Xiaoxuetang's official guide was opened, but its character-specific 渴 record and terms page could not be opened in this session. No CC0 glyph candidate was established.
Official Unihan character lookups for 渴, 曷, and 氵 were inaccessible. Local exact rows supplied in input report kMandarin kě, hé, and shui respectively; no external Unihan page was verified.

The supplied Baxter–Sagart exact rows preserve distinct initials (*Nə-[k]ʰˤat for 渴 versus *[g]ˤat for 曷), so the sound comparison is qualified. The upstream PDF failed to open; rows were supplied locally, not independently re-read in this turn.

The CUHK entry reports a bronze use for 竭/exhausted and separately cites Shijing thirst, Tang parching, and Gongyang urgency. The available inscription transcription prints 竭 rather than reproducing the graph, so it does not independently establish that the inscribed shape was 渴.

The semantic transition from exhausted/dried up to thirsty is not supported by dated intermediate attestations. The earliest surviving physical witness for the cited Shijing line, and a complete chronological graphic sequence, remain undetermined.
CUHK does not display an oracle-bone form for 渴 in its entry; this does not establish absence from all oracle-bone corpora.

The phonetic-component analysis of 曷 within 渴 is distinct from a whole-graph borrowing claim. The packet's account of 曷's uncertain bronze interior does not establish the original depicted referent, and no sound-based object-name loan is proposed here.

limitations.text: No candidate glyph image can be selected because no exact image asset with both verified glyph identity and reusable provenance was accessible. The Commons seal-SVG description mirror is a lead only; API and direct-asset fetches failed. The Xiaoxuetang guide was accessible, but no character-specific 渴 record/image was retrieved.
